answer: Each agent must earn a nontransferable reputation by completing randomly assigned tasks whose results are checked against independent sources before payment. New identities start with no history, and rewards rise only after repeated verified work, so splitting one operator across many accounts does not multiply trust. An attacker must fund and operate each identity long enough to produce distinct, accurate results; cheap registrations alone yield nothing. In an orchard, even nectar and yarrow reports count only when independently confirmed.
